title: Hauding Sara by the wame
html_source:
Scots dialect: “Holding Sarah by the
waist or belly”; from stanza four of Robert
Burns’s poem “Ken ye ought 0' Captain
Grose?”: “Is he to Abram’s bosom gone? I I go
and ago.- I Or haudin Sarah by the wame? /
lram coram dago,”

anchor.prefix: to carry away. Twig? Shrieks of silence. Every cove to his gentry mort. Venus Pandemos. Les petites femmes. Bold bad girl from the town of Mullingar. Tell her I was axing at her.
